title: Shop owners:
6 prompts to *save*
at the counter
slides.sub: Copy, paste, fill the brackets. Free ChatGPT or Gemini, on your phone.

slides.name: The price *reply*
slides.line: Turns a one-word 'price?' message into a polite reply that can close the sale.

rows.v: The product and your real price

slides.box: A customer sent 'price?' on WhatsApp for [product]. Write a short, polite Hinglish reply: the price is ₹[your price], one line on what's included, and ask if I should keep one aside. Under 40 words.
slides.catch: Type your real price in. Never let it guess.

slides.name: The offer *board*
slides.line: Writes your offer in Hindi and English, short enough for a board or WhatsApp status.

rows.v: Festival offer, new stock, weekend sale
Copy the best option onto your board

slides.box: Write 3 options for a shop offer board. Each: one Hindi line in Devanagari, then the same in English, under 8 words each. Offer: [your offer]. Valid till [date]. Keep it clear, no exaggeration.
slides.catch: Ask a Hindi reader to check the spellings.

slides.name: The reorder *list*
slides.line: Turns your scribbled sales notes into a clean list of what to reorder.

rows.v: Closing time, before you call the supplier
Type your notes, or attach a clear photo

slides.box: These are today's sales notes from my shop: [type or paste notes]. Make a table: item, how many sold, reorder yes or check. Say yes only where I wrote 'khatam' or 'low'. Don't add items I didn't write.
slides.catch: It can't see your shelf. Count before ordering.

slides.name: The udhaar *reminder*
slides.line: Asks for pending money politely, so the customer pays and still comes back.

rows.v: Udhaar pending for more than a week

slides.box: Write a polite WhatsApp reminder in Hinglish to [name], a regular customer. ₹[amount] is pending since [date]. Friendly, never rude. Say UPI to [your UPI ID] works. Under 50 words. Give a soft and a firmer version.
slides.catch: Check the amount against your khata first.

slides.name: The review *reply*
slides.line: Writes a calm owner's reply to any Google Maps review, good or bad.

rows.v: Any new review, especially a complaint
Your Business Profile, Reviews, then Reply

slides.box: I own [shop name]. Write my reply to this Google Maps review: [paste review]. Thank them by name, answer their main point honestly, and if it's a complaint, say sorry once and invite them back. Under 60 words. Promise nothing I didn't say.
slides.catch: Replying needs a verified Google Business Profile.

slides.name: The *translator*
slides.line: Tells you what a customer wrote in a language you can't read, then translates your reply.

rows.v: A message in a language you don't read

slides.box: A customer sent me this: [paste message]. Tell me in simple Hindi what they want, in one line. Then translate my reply into their language, simple and polite: [type your reply in Hindi].
slides.catch: Double-check names, numbers and addresses it translates.

slides.title: Save these *6.*
items: 'Price?' reply that can close the sale
Sales notes into a reorder list
The catch: check every price and number before you send

slides.title: Send this to *the uncle*
slides.who: who types every reply with one finger.
slides.text: and I'll DM you all 6 prompts, ready to copy
slides.catch: AI doesn't know your stock or prices. Check every number.
